# ATLAS - Deployment Guide

## Quick Deploy Options

### 1. Render.com (Easiest - Free Tier Available)

```bash
# 1. Push to GitHub
git add . && git commit -m "deploy" && git push origin main

# 2. Connect to Render
# Go to https://dashboard.render.com → New → Blueprint
# Select your repo → Uses render.yaml automatically

# 3. Add environment variables in Render dashboard:
# - AUTH_SECRET_KEY: (generate with: openssl rand -base64 32)
# - DATABASE_PASSWORD: (auto-generated by Render Postgres)
# - REDIS_PASSWORD: (auto-generated by Render Redis)
```

**What Render creates:**
- Backend API (auto-scaling)
- Frontend (static site with Nginx)
- PostgreSQL database
- Redis cache
- All connected via internal network

---

### 2. Fly.io (Great for Containers)

```bash
# 1. Install flyctl
curl -L https://fly.io/install.sh | sh

# 2. Login
fly auth login

# 3. Create Postgres
fly postgres create --name atlas-db --region ord

# 4. Create Redis
fly redis create --name atlas-redis --region ord

# 5. Set secrets (get passwords from steps 3-4)
fly secrets set \
  DATABASE_PASSWORD=<postgres-password> \
  REDIS_PASSWORD=<redis-password> \
  AUTH_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH=/app/keys/private.pem \
  AUTH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH=/app/keys/public.pem

# 6. Deploy
fly deploy --config fly.toml
```

---

### 3. Docker Compose (VPS / EC2 / DigitalOcean)

```bash
# 1. On server, install Docker & Docker Compose
# Ubuntu:
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y docker.io docker-compose-plugin

# 2. Clone repo
git clone <your-repo> atlas && cd atlas

# 3. Generate keys
./scripts/generate-keys.sh

# 4. Configure .env
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with production values:
# - ENVIRONMENT=production
# - DEBUG=false
# - AUTH_SECRET_KEY=<strong-random-key>
# - DATABASE_PASSWORD=<strong-password>
# - CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://yourdomain.com

# 5. Start
docker-compose up -d

# 6. Verify
docker-compose ps
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

**With Nginx Reverse Proxy (for SSL):**

```nginx
# /etc/nginx/sites-available/atlas
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name yourdomain.com;
    return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name yourdomain.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/privkey.pem;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:3000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location /api {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:8000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location /ws {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}
```

```bash
# Install Certbot & get SSL
sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx
sudo certbot --nginx -d yourdomain.com
```

### 4. Kubernetes (Production Scale)

```bash
# Using the Helm chart (create one from the K8s manifests)
# See k8s/ directory for manifests

# Apply in order:
kubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/secrets.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/postgres.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/redis.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/backend.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/frontend.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/ingress.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/hpa.yaml
```

## Required Environment Variables (Production)

| Variable | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | ✅ |
| `DEBUG` | `false` | ✅ |
| `AUTH_SECRET_KEY` | 32+ char random string | ✅ |
| `AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` | `/app/keys/private.pem` | ✅ |
| `AUTH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH` | `/app/keys/public.pem` | ✅ |
| `DATABASE_HOST` | Postgres host | ✅ |
| `DATABASE_PORT` | `5432` | ✅ |
| `DATABASE_USERNAME` | `postgres` | ✅ |
| `DATABASE_PASSWORD` | Strong password | ✅ |
| `DATABASE_NAME` | `atlas` | ✅ |
| `REDIS_HOST` | Redis host | ✅ |
| `REDIS_PORT` | `6379` | ✅ |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | If Redis has auth | |
| `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` | `["https://yourdomain.com"]` | ✅ |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `sendgrid`/`ses`/`smtp` | |
| `EMAIL_SENDGRID_API_KEY` | If using SendGrid | |
| `AI_OPENAI_API_KEY` | If using OpenAI | |
| `MONITORING_SENTRY_DSN` | Error tracking | |
| `STORAGE_PROVIDER` | `s3`/`gcs`/`azure` | |
| `STORAGE_BUCKET` | Bucket name | |

---

## Pre-Deploy Checklist

- [ ] Generate JWT keys: `./scripts/generate-keys.sh`
- [ ] Set `ENVIRONMENT=production`
- [ ] Set `DEBUG=false`
- [ ] Generate strong `AUTH_SECRET_KEY` (32+ chars)
- [ ] Configure PostgreSQL with SSL
- [ ] Configure Redis with password
- [ ] Set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to your domain only
- [ ] Configure email provider (SendGrid/SES)
- [ ] Set up S3/GCS for file uploads
- [ ] Configure Sentry for error tracking
- [ ] Set up monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana)
- [ ] Configure backup strategy for PostgreSQL
- [ ] Test health endpoints: `/health`, `/health/ready`
- [ ] Run migrations: `alembic upgrade head`

---

## Post-Deploy Verification

```bash
# 1. Health checks
curl https://yourdomain.com/health
curl https://yourdomain.com/health/ready

# 2. API docs
open https://yourdomain.com/docs

# 3. Frontend
open https://yourdomain.com

# 4. Flower (Celery monitoring)
open https://yourdomain.com:5555

# 5. Test auth flow
curl -X POST https://yourdomain.com/api/v1/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Test","slug":"test","admin_email":"test@example.com","admin_password":"SecurePass123!","admin_first_name":"Test","admin_last_name":"User"}'
```

## Monitoring Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `/health` | Liveness probe |
| `/health/ready` | Readiness probe |
| `/metrics` | Prometheus metrics |
| `/api/v1/monitoring/status` | System status |

---

## Backup Strategy

```bash
# Daily PostgreSQL backup (run via cron)
0 2 * * * docker exec atlas-postgres pg_dump -U postgres atlas | gzip > /backups/atlas_$(date +\%Y\%m\%d).sql.gz

# Weekly full backup to S3
0 3 * * 0 aws s3 cp /backups/atlas_$(date -d '7 days ago' +\%Y\%m\%d).sql.gz s3://your-backup-bucket/
```

---

## Scaling Guide

| Component | Horizontal Scaling |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Backend API | Add replicas, use sticky sessions for WebSocket |
| Celery Workers | Increase `--concurrency` or add worker pods |
| Celery Beat | Single instance (leader election) |
| PostgreSQL | Read replicas, connection pooling (PgBouncer) |
| Redis | Redis Cluster or Sentinel |
| Frontend | Static files on CDN (CloudFront/Cloudflare) |

---

## Support

- **Logs**: `docker-compose logs -f backend` or `fly logs -a atlas-recruitment`
- **Database**: `docker-compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -d atlas`
- **Redis**: `docker-compose exec redis redis-cli`
- **Flower**: `https://yourdomain.com:5555`
